title: New Year's Questions: stage-by-stage questions for founders instead of resolutions
summary: Jason argues resolutions fail and suggests asking yourself sharp, stage-specific questions instead. For bootstrappers, consultants, new startups, post-PMF and scale-phase companies, he lists the levers that matter: price, retention, marketing, focus, ICP alignment, hiring and unit economics.

principles.text: To double bootstrapped profits, raise price before cutting costs, improve retention before new markets, and invest in marketing before features.
principles.quote: it's usually increasing price, not cutting costs, and usually increasing retention, not expanding to new markets, and usually better marketing, not more features

principles.text: Ask what single spend could be game-changing, and consider paid marketing may deserve more money than you think.
principles.quote: what's the *single* most impactful thing you could spend non-trivial money on? For example, could you be spending more than you think on something like paid-marketing?

principles.text: Test your consulting rates by imagining you had to double them: what would you change in positioning, website and service to justify it?
principles.quote: If I *forced* you to double your rates, what would you have to do to justify it?

principles.text: New companies should immediately try to get 20 people to pay $50, and be completely honest about what the market says, price included.
principles.quote: How can you get 20 people to give you $50?

principles.text: After product/market fit, align the whole company on one most-important thing and one clarified target customer, saying no to distractions.
principles.quote: if I asked any employee what's the one thing the company has to do to be successful, they'd all have the same reply?

principles.text: In scale-phase, focus on what will be critical in three months: today's minor irritants become massive, and spend disproportionate time hiring 10xers.
principles.quote: what is only of minor importance today will be trivial in three months, whereas what is important but a minor irritant today will become critical and massive in three months
